raw_response:
I have been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father farmed it too. I am 60 years old and my back is not what it was, but I know this land. I know what grows here.

In Quzhou, everyone grows wheat in winter and corn in summer on the same fields. That is the rotation. That is what makes sense. The soil here is flat and deep. We have the well and the pump to irrigate. There is no reason to change.

I have about 8 mu of field. I will plant all of it in wheat around October when the ground cools. I use the Jimai variety — the seed station has been selling it for years and my neighbors use it. It gives good yield and does not fall over in wind.

For fertilizer, I mix diammonium phosphate and potassium sulfate into the base dressing before I rotary till, then I add urea in April when the wheat starts jointing. I always add a bit more urea than the extension people say — I have seen what happens when wheat goes yellow in spring.

I irrigate wheat three times: once in November to help roots before winter, once in April at jointing, once in May before heading. If it is very dry I may add one more but usually three is enough.

After wheat harvest in June I go straight to corn. I do not plow again — I plant directly into the stubble with my seeder. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, same as everyone here. I put phosphate fertilizer down at planting, then broadcast urea when the corn is knee-high. Summer has rain so I usually only pump water twice — once if it is dry at silking, sometimes once more at grain fill.

I spray herbicide in both crops. In wheat I also spray for aphids and mildew in May. In corn I spray for weeds early and watch for borer.

This is what I will do. Same as last year.
